description.html: This method loads a machine learning model that finds hands in a video, giving you the position of 21 points on each hand (fingertips, knuckles and wrist). The model runs in your browser, so your video is never sent anywhere. This method comes from the netnet-machine-learning extension, so it only works if you load its script after nn's.

description.html: This method loads a machine learning model that finds faces in a video, giving you the position of 478 points on each face, and optionally scores for its expression (like a smile or an open mouth). The model runs in your browser, so your video is never sent anywhere. This method comes from the netnet-machine-learning extension, so it only works if you load its script after nn's.

description.html: This method loads a machine learning model that finds a body in a video, giving you the position of 33 points from face to feet. The model runs in your browser, so your video is never sent anywhere. This method comes from the netnet-machine-learning extension, so it only works if you load its script after nn's.

description.html: This method sends a message to a large language model (LLM) and gives you its reply. The model can run locally on your own computer (with Ollama or another local provider), or in the cloud (with Gemini, Anthropic or OpenAI, using your own API key). This method comes from the netnet-machine-learning extension, so it only works if you load its script after nn's.

description.html: This method runs the model on the current frame of a video and returns what it found (hands, faces or bodies), each as a list of points on the page. Call it every frame, inside your animation loop.

description.html: The full, raw output from the model you loaded with nn.hands(), nn.face() or nn.pose(), for the latest frame it looked at. It includes extras that detect() leaves out, like how confident the model is about what it found.
